Class RawRequestOptions

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.http.client.RawRequestOptions
public final class RawRequestOptions extends Object
Options for a single RawHttpClient exchange, see RawHttpClient.exchange(io.micronaut.http.HttpRequest, io.micronaut.http.body.CloseableByteBody, Thread, RawRequestOptions).

getDefault() behaves like RawHttpClient.exchange(io.micronaut.http.HttpRequest, io.micronaut.http.body.CloseableByteBody, Thread). proxy() is the preset for relaying a request to an upstream server unchanged: redirects are passed back to the caller and encoded response bytes are not decompressed. A proxy removes the hop-by-hop headers itself, see HttpHeadersUtil.stripHopByHopHeaders(io.micronaut.http.MutableHttpHeaders).

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • isFollowRedirects

      public boolean isFollowRedirects()
      Whether redirects are followed, if the client is configured to follow them. If false, a redirect response is returned to the caller. Defaults to true.
      Returns:
      Whether redirects are followed

    • isRetainHostHeader

      public boolean isRetainHostHeader()
      Whether the Host header of the request is sent as given. If false, it is removed and computed from the request URI. Defaults to true: like an exchange without options, the header is only computed when the request has none.

      The JDK client can only send a Host header when the jdk.httpclient.allowRestrictedHeaders system property includes host, and fails the exchange otherwise.

      Returns:
      Whether the host header is retained

    • isDecompress

      public boolean isDecompress()
      Whether the response body is decompressed, if the client is configured to decompress. If false, an encoded response is returned with its Content-Encoding header and its bytes unchanged. Defaults to true.
      Returns:
      Whether the response is decompressed

    • getResponseTimeout

      public @Nullable Duration getResponseTimeout()
      The maximum time to wait for the response headers, or null for no limit other than the client's read timeout. It can only shorten the wait: the read timeout of the client still applies, also to the reads of the response body. When it elapses, the exchange fails with a ReadTimeoutException.
      Returns:
      The response timeout
